reqCondGroup.reqCond: You are on duty, with your call sign entered.
You know the call sign of the incoming operator.

reqSupportEquips.supportEquipDescr: A computer or phone with a web browser, on the same network as the server

caution.warningAndCautionPara: The report shows the console as it is when you sign. Acknowledge or deal with alerts first, so the incoming operator does not inherit work you could have finished.

proceduralStep.para: On the Console tab, acknowledge every open alert you have seen. Refer to .
Select the Shift handover tab. Read the Handover report. Check that it matches what you know of the shift.
In Notes for the next operator, write what the incoming operator needs to know. Include:

listItem.para: any alert you shelved, and why;
anything to check at a set time, such as a pass or a limit review.

note.notePara: Notes are shared and saved as you type.

proceduralStep.para: Type the incoming operator's call sign in Incoming operator.
If the team keeps handover reports elsewhere, select Copy and paste the report where it is needed.

note.notePara: Do this before you sign. Signing clears the notes field.

proceduralStep.para: Check that the message confirms the incoming operator is on duty.

note.notePara: Signing writes a fingerprint of the report, your notes, both call signs and the number of unacknowledged alerts to the audit trail.

reqCondGroup.reqCond: The incoming operator is shown as on duty, and the handover is signed in the audit trail.
